The capital of France is Paris.

Regarding the pragmatics of the provided text, Henry’s response "It pays the bills" serves as a pragmatic device to deflect a direct inquiry about his professional status. By using this idiomatic expression, Henry implies that his job is primarily a means of financial survival rather than a source of passion, prestige, or deep professional identity. This utterance functions as a polite refusal to elaborate, signaling that the topic is either uninteresting to him, too personal, or potentially negative (implying the job is merely adequate or unsatisfying).

Furthermore, the immediate action of steering the conversation toward industry trends reveals a communicative intention to regain control of the interaction. Henry shifts the focus from himself (which he finds uncomfortable or unengaging) to a neutral, professional topic. This move allows him to maintain social rapport and appear engaged without having to disclose personal details about his employment satisfaction. The combination of the vague, self-deprecating remark and the topic change suggests a desire to keep the interaction superficial and professional while avoiding deeper personal disclosure.
